description: Find things worth photographing by name instead of by OpenStreetMap tag, with automatic failover across Overpass mirrors.

tools.name: geocoding_search
tools.description: Resolve a free-text place name to coordinates using OpenStreetMap's Nominatim geocoder. Required: q, the place name (e.g. 'San Pedro, CA'). Optional: countrycodes to restrict matches to ISO-3166 alpha-2 codes (e.g. 'us,ca'), limit for how many matches to return (default 5), and format (json, jsonv2, or geojson; default json). Returns an array of matches ordered by worldwide relevance, each with lat, lon, a display name, and a bounding box. Keyless, but Nominatim permits only about one request per second. Prefer the `near` and `route` commands when the goal is finding subjects — they geocode internally. Call this first when a place name is ambiguous, then pass the chosen lat/lon to overpass_query.

params.name: q
params.description: Free-text place name, e.g. 'San Pedro, CA'

params.name: countrycodes
params.description: Restrict to ISO-3166 alpha-2 codes, comma separated, e.g. us,ca

tools.name: overpass_query
tools.description: Run a raw Overpass QL program against OpenStreetMap and return the matching elements. Required: data, a complete Overpass QL program (e.g. '[out:json][timeout:25];nwr(around:5000,34.05,-118.24)['man_made'='water_tower'];out center 5;'). Returns the Overpass JSON envelope with an elements array; ways and relations carry a center point when the program ends in `out center`. This is the escape hatch for queries the curated subject taxonomy does not cover — prefer the `near`, `route`, and `geojson` commands for ordinary use, since they build correct QL, fail over across mirrors, and cache results. Call geocoding_search first if you have a place name rather than coordinates. Note that Overpass signals overload with an HTTP 200 carrying an HTML page rather than an error status.

params.name: data
params.description: An Overpass QL program, e.g. [out:json][timeout:25];nwr(around:5000,34.05,-118.24)['man_made'='water_tower'];out center;

tools.name: overpass_status
tools.description: Report one Overpass mirror's current rate-limit budget and running queries. Takes no parameters. Returns plain text, not JSON: the announced endpoint, the rate limit, how many query slots are free right now, and any queries currently running. Useful for checking whether a mirror has capacity before sending an expensive query. Prefer the `mirrors` command when the question is which host to use — it probes every mirror in the failover list concurrently and returns a comparable table; this tool reports on the single configured endpoint.
